newsitem.title: NORWAY: Sentiment positive on Oslo bourse, market edges up.
newsitem.headline: Sentiment positive on Oslo bourse, market edges up.

text.p: Norwegian shares advanced on Monday, regaining the ground lost after the political uncertainty of last week when Norway got a new prime minister and government.
Traders said sentiment was positive and the market was expected to remain on an upward path.
Oslo's Total share index climbed 0.46 percent to 876.92 points in turnover of 778 million crowns.
Trade in construction and offshore group Aker accounted for more than 25 percent of total volume at 201 million crowns due to options being exercised on expiry.
Aker, soon to merge with investment group RGI, ended unchanged at 135 crowns.
Kvaerner climbed strongly to 240 crowns, a gain of 11 crowns, in small volume.
"Kvaerner was up but there was no special news out on the company. The volume indicates that someone wanted the stock and there weren't many sellers," said one broker.

Telecommunications group Nera put on two crowns to end at 220.50 crowns in turnover of 30.1 million crowns. The company presented nine-month results slightly below expectations but with a positive forecast for the fourth quarter.
